opportunities.title: The Trezor Pattern: Three Breaches in a Year Means the Problem Isn't the Vendor, It's the Supply Chain
opportunities.why_now: Trezor just disclosed its third partner data leak in 2026, this time via shipping partner Skladon affecting 27,000 orders.
opportunities.angle: Explainer/trend piece connecting the three Trezor incidents as a supply-chain security failure, with a checklist for hardware wallet buyers on what 'customer data exposed' actually puts at risk (phishing, physical targeting).

opportunities.title: 178 Sites, One Skimmer: How HSBC, Ledger and BBC Got the Same Malware
opportunities.why_now: A single supply-chain compromise just hit 178 major websites simultaneously with credit-card and crypto-stealing code, blending TradFi and crypto victims in one breach.
opportunities.angle: Incident breakdown with technical specifics (what the injected script targets, how it exfiltrates wallet data) and a 'you already knew this was coming' framing on third-party JS dependencies as the weakest link.

opportunities.title: Google Just Confirmed What We Said: AI Agents Are Now Finding Your Zero-Days For You
opportunities.why_now: Google disclosed hackers are using autonomous AI agents to discover and exploit software vulnerabilities at scale, a structural shift in attacker economics.
opportunities.angle: Thesis piece/X thread arguing this changes the security math for every protocol and wallet — patch cycles are now the bottleneck, not discovery; tie to Luxor CEO's 'AI dark forest' comment for a second source.

opportunities.title: Safe Lost $6.5M to a Compromised Key — Again. Multisig Was Never the Fix
opportunities.why_now: Safe wallet reportedly lost $6.5M with Zodiac suspects pointing to key compromise, just months after the much larger Bybit-linked Safe incident earlier in the year.
opportunities.angle: Security-led postmortem on why key custody, not contract logic, keeps being the failure point in 'safe' multisig setups — actionable signing-hygiene takeaways for treasuries.

opportunities.title: The Binance Hacker Just Moved $63M After Going Quiet for Two Weeks — Here's What the Silence Meant
opportunities.why_now: The Binance hacker resumed moving $63M in stolen ETH after a two-week pause, reigniting the custody debate FalconX flagged days earlier.
opportunities.angle: Forensic/market-structure angle tracing the laundering pause-and-move pattern, paired with the FalconX custody thesis — argue this is the event that finally pushes institutions off exchange custody.
